title: The Sikh Gurus

cards.b: The ten Gurus built a distinct faith, scripture and later a political power. Prelims asks about each Guru’s contribution and Mughal confrontations. It links with Bhakti and the Punjab freedom struggle.

Born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib). Taught Ik Onkar, equality, naam japna, kirat karna, vand chakna. Founded Kartarpur (on the Ravi), started langar. Rejected caste, idols, asceticism. Four udasis (journeys). Succeeded by Angad.

Angad (2nd) devised Gurmukhi script. Amar Das (3rd) institutionalised langar, set up manjis, opposed sati and purdah; Akbar visited him. Ram Das (4th) founded Amritsar (land from Akbar) and the Harmandir sarovar, started the masand system. The Guruship became hereditary after him.

Compiled the Adi Granth (1604) with verses of Gurus, Kabir, Ravidas, Farid. Completed the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) in 1604, founded Tarn Taran and Kartarpur (Jalandhar). Executed in 1606 under Jahangir (supporting Khusrau). Considered the first martyr.

Hargobind (6th) wore two swords (miri and piri), built the Akal Takht, fought Mughal forces. Har Rai (7th) and Har Krishan (8th; child Guru). Tegh Bahadur (9th) founded Anandpur Sahib; he was executed at Delhi in 1675 under Aurangzeb for defending Kashmiri Pandits’ right to worship (Gurdwara Sis Ganj).

On Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur he founded the Khalsa with the Panj Pyare and the Five Ks (kesh, kangha, kara, kirpan, kachera). Surname Singh and Kaur. Battles at Bhangani and Chamkaur. Composed the Dasam Granth; ended the line of living Gurus, declaring the Guru Granth Sahib to be Guru (1708, Nanded). Banda Singh Bahadur led the next phase.

Banda Singh Bahadur (1708 to 1716) captured Sirhind. Misls (12 confederacies) and then Maharaja Ranjit Singh (r. 1799 to 1839) built the Sikh Empire from Lahore, with the Anglo-Sikh wars (1845–46; 1848–49) ending it. The Singh Sabha (1873) and Akali movement (Gurdwara Reform Act, 1925; SGPC) followed.

W. H. McLeod argued that early Sikhism was a movement of the Sant tradition (like Kabir), that later became militant. Others (Harbans Singh) stress continuity of spiritual-political thought from Nanak. The sources for the early period are also debated.

The Kartarpur Corridor (Gurdaspur to Pakistan’s Kartarpur Sahib) opened in November 2019 for Guru Nanak’s 550th birth anniversary. Veer Bal Diwas is observed on 26 December for the Sahibzade. The Golden Temple’s langar serves tens of thousands daily. Punjabi in Gurmukhi is a constitutional language.
